column1: # Held-out list, group nordic (Nordic ISPs, mail providers and web hosts), for the M2 autodetect measurement (card ML-097).

# Researched on 2026-10-05 (07:49:25Z to 08:11:35Z UTC) by one agent that only ran web searches and read public web pages (providers' help pages, press, registry and third-party pages, each named in the evidence column).
# Not done for any domain: DNS lookups (dig/host/nslookup/DoH), requests to autoconfig.<domain>, autoconfig.thunderbird.net or /.well-known/autoconfig, connections to mail ports, logins.

# Incidental requests: one HTTPS GET to privat.globalconnect.no (a guessed consumer-site name; it did not resolve) and one HTTPS GET on port 443 to mail.sol.dk before the sol.dk FAQ showed that name is its IMAP host (it redirected to www.sol.dk).
# Several rows' own websites (www.inet.fi, www.sol.dk, www.wemail.no, www.inbox.com) were read for their FAQ pages; every page read resolves the web host name it fetches.

# Selection, largest first per country: Norway: Norid's top-10 .no registrars (CSV export of https://www.norid.no/en/om-domenenavn/statistics/key-figures/ read 2026-10-05: Domeneshop, Group.One, One.com, Webhuset, Domene, Name SRS AB, Ascio, Abion, GoDaddy, Telenor Norge)

#   are all used already, wholesale/brand-protection registrars, global, or (Telenor) mail on online.no; syse.no and fastname.no now redirect to uniweb.no; the big ISPs' mail domains are all used (Telenor online.no, Altibox, Telia getmail.no, NextGenTel broadpark.no per https://hjelp.nextgentel.no/no_NO/e-post/oppsett-av-e-post);

#   GlobalConnect's consumer customer-service pages (https://globalconnect.no/kundeservice/) and Eviny's FAQ (https://www.eviny.no/kundeservice/sporsmal-og-svar) have no e-mail section, so the Norwegian rows are mail providers, a closed provider and the next host (STW).

#   Sweden: Telia and Com Hem used; Telenor (bredband.net), Bahnhof, and Loopia (largest .se registrar). Denmark: YouSee used; Norlys/Stofa (stofanet.dk), Telenor DK's sitemap (https://www.telenor.dk/sitemap/) has no mail-setup page; SOL.dk portal mail.
#   Finland: Elisa and DNA used; Telia's inet.fi. Iceland: Siminn used; Syn (internet.is) and the host 1984. Market rankings beyond the Norid list were not verified.
# Caveat: wemail.no, inbox.com, inet.fi and sol.dk are brands of one operator, Inbox.com AS (Norway), with the same FAQ template, so results on them are correlated.
# Columns: domain, group, expect (settings|unsupported|no-mail|unknown), imap, smtp, evidence.
# Endpoint: host:port:tls|starttls:users, users = addr | local | other | local/addr; ' ; ' separates endpoints.
runbox.com
column6: https://help.runbox.com/email-program-settings/ (article modified 2025-01-30, read 2026-10-05): table IMAP mail.runbox.com 993 TLS/SSL, SMTP mail.runbox.com 465 TLS/SSL and 587 STARTTLS, password authentication; Usernames section: for an address Runbox gave you, the username is the full @runbox.com address or just the part before @ (both documented, hence local/addr); alias addresses cannot log in (an alias would be other); synonymous domains include runbox.no; https://help.runbox.com/smtp/ and https://help.runbox.com/imap/ (read 2026-10-05) repeat 587 STARTTLS or 465 TLS/SSL and 993 SSL; https://runbox.com/about/ (read 2026-10-05): Runbox Solutions AS, headquarters in Oslo, Norway; selection: Norwegian mail provider

column1: wemail.no
column6: https://www.wemail.no/faq (read 2026-10-05; the FAQ text is in the page's embedded Next.js data): answer to the mail-program question: incoming Vertsnavn mail.wemail.no, Brukernavn = your @wemail.no address, Tjenerport 993, SSL: On; outgoing smtp.wemail.no, same username, port 465, SSL: On; server requires authentication; no 143 or 587 named on this page (not recorded; the sister site inbox.com lists STARTTLS on 143/587 for its own service); 'Hvem eier Wemail?': Inbox.com AS; https://www.tek.no/nyheter/nyhet/i/Qml8dx/get-overfoerte-kundene-sine-til-epostselskap-som-naa-vil-ha-betalt-forkastelig-sier-kunde (published 2020-09-18, read 2026-10-05 via a summarizing fetch): Get (now Telia Norge) moved its Getmail customers, about 25,000 active accounts, to Wemail, a Norwegian ad-free mail service then run by Recurrent AS, in summer 2020; whether @getmail.no addresses now use these servers is not stated; caveat: same operator and template as inbox.com, inet.fi and sol.dk

column1: inbox.com
column6: https://www.inbox.com/faq (read 2026-10-05, embedded FAQ data): 'I am using an email client or app. What settings should I use?': incoming hostname mail.inbox.com, username = the full @inbox.com address, port 993 with SSL/TLS (or 143 with STARTTLS); outgoing smtp.inbox.com, same username, port 465 with SSL/TLS (or 587 with STARTTLS), authentication required; https://www.inbox.com/faq/technical (read 2026-10-05): IMAP plain or STARTTLS on 143, implicit TLS 993; SMTP plain or STARTTLS on 25 and 587, implicit TLS 465 (25 not recorded: no host named and not in the client answer); custom domains are not hosted; mail is stored on MailCore's infrastructure in Denmark; https://www.inbox.com/corp (read 2026-10-05): Inbox.com AS, founded 2018, headquartered in Oslo, postal address Asker, Norway, 14 consumer brands; fjordmail.com redirects to www.inbox.com; counted as Norwegian because of the operator (the domain itself is an old international brand); caveat: same operator and template as wemail.no, inet.fi and sol.dk

column1: myopera.com
column6: My Opera Mail (Opera Software ASA, Norwegian) closed: https://web.archive.org/web/20131031211626/http://my.opera.com/chooseopera/blog/2013/10/31/important-announcement-about-your-my-opera-account (Opera's announcement of 2013-10-31, archived copy read 2026-10-05): My Opera shuts down as of March 1, 2014, and to 'What will happen with my My Opera email?' it answers that the service will be discontinued along with My Opera; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Opera (read 2026-10-05): My Opera belonged to Opera Software ASA; My Opera Mail launched 2011-04-07 on Opera's FastMail platform; the site closed 2014-03-03; https://www.techspot.com/news/43204-opera-launches-new-webmail-service-my-opera-mail.html (2011-04-08, read 2026-10-05): every My Opera account got an @myopera.com address through mail.opera.com; whether anything at myopera.com accepts mail today was not checked (no DNS lookups)

column1: servetheworld.net
column6: WEAK: ServeTheWorld (STW, Norwegian host; its brand site https://stw.no/no/ read 2026-10-05 gives its own contact addresses at servetheworld.net) documents two mail products and does not say which one its own domain uses. STW Mail (Open-Xchange): https://faq.servetheworld.net/myserve/no/stwmail.md (dated 2026-09-18) and https://faq.servetheworld.net/myserve/en/stwmail.md (read 2026-10-05): IMAP imap.stw.no 993 SSL/TLS; SMTP smtp.stw.no '465 eller 587', SSL/TLS on 465 or StartTLS on 587; username = your e-mail address; its SRV examples repeat imaps 993 imap.stw.no, smtps 465 and submission 587 smtp.stw.no. Web-hosting mail: https://faq.servetheworld.net/myserve/en/webhotell/epost.md (dated 2026-09-17) and https://faq.servetheworld.net/myserve/en/webhotell/epost/thunderbird.md (dated 2026-09-18, read 2026-10-05): username = full address, IMAP and SMTP host = your-domain or mail.your-domain, IMAP 993 SSL/TLS, SMTP 465 SSL/TLS; the servetheworld.net and mail.servetheworld.net endpoints are derived from that per-customer pattern for the host's own domain; selection: STW is listed among Norway-headquartered hosts by https://www.whtop.com/directory/country/no/category/domains (read via a summarizing fetch) and is the first one there not already used

column1: loopia.se
column6: https://support.loopia.se/wiki/e-postservrar/ (modified 2026-09-15, read 2026-10-05): username is always the full e-mail address, authentication required for outgoing mail; incoming mailcluster.loopia.se, IMAP 143 'ingen kryptering / STARTTLS', IMAP 993 SSL/TLS; outgoing mailcluster.loopia.se, 587 'ingen kryptering / STARTTLS', 465 SSL/TLS (143 and 587 recorded as starttls, their plaintext use not recorded); always use SSL/TLS or STARTTLS is recommended; https://support.loopia.com/wiki/email-servers/ (modified 2026-09-30, read 2026-10-05) says the same in English; the Norwegian page https://support.loopia.no/wiki/e-postservere/ (modified 2016-01-07, read 2026-10-05) still labels 143/587 'uten SSL' and lists 465 or 'alternativt 587 for visse klienter' under 'Med SSL' (older wording); the docs cover customer mailboxes; that Loopia's own loopia.se addresses use the same cluster is assumed; selection: https://www.loopia.com/domainnames/se-domains/ (read 2026-10-05) says Loopia is the largest .se agent and registers more than 30% of .se domains

column1: bahnhof.se
column6: WEAK: https://bahnhof.se/privat/kundservice/ (modified 2026-09-29, read 2026-10-05), section 'Kom igang med din e-post': broadband customers get an e-mail service run in Sweden and create addresses on Mina sidor; IMAP (recommended): incoming imap.privat.bahnhof.se (port 993, SSL), outgoing mailout.privat.bahnhof.se (port 465, SSL); POP3 pop3.privat.bahnhof.se 995 SSL; webmail epost.bahnhof.se; no 587 documented; the page names neither the domain customer addresses are on nor the username form (hence local/addr); this row uses Bahnhof's own domain (its customer-service address is at bahnhof.se), customer addresses may be on another domain (the page also says customers get a free .st domain with a web account); older PDF guides under https://www.bahnhof.se/filestorage/userfiles/epostomlaggning/ found by web search now return an HTML page and were not usable; selection: large Swedish ISP after Telia, Com Hem and Telenor (ranking not verified)

column1: bredband.net
column6: WEAK: Telenor Sverige (formerly Bredbandsbolaget) consumer mail; no official documentation found on 2026-10-05: the telenor.se sitemap index https://www.telenor.se/sitemap-index.xml and its child sitemaps (online-sales, my-telenor-web; read 2026-10-05) list no e-mail help page, and web searches found no Telenor page or press item; the only source found, https://smtpedia.com/bredbandsbolaget-se-email-settings-pop3-imap-smtp/ (third party, read 2026-10-05 via a summarizing fetch), claims Telenor announced the end of its consumer webmail in September 2023 and deleted all @bredband.net and @bredbandsbolaget.se addresses on 2023-11-15, but cites no source, so it is not used as no-mail ground truth; selection: Telenor is the next big Swedish ISP after Telia and Com Hem (both used)

column1: stofanet.dk
column6: WEAK: Norlys (formerly Stofa) mail: https://norlys.dk/kundeservice/internet/kom-godt-i-gang/norlys-mail/ (read 2026-10-05; guide texts from the page's embedded data): setup guides are 'only relevant if you became a customer before June 2024'; Norlys-mail was formerly Stofa-mail and closes six months after the internet subscription ends; iPhone guide: incoming and outgoing host mail.mailnorlys.dk, username = the full Norlys mail address, no ports; Android guide: incoming mail.mailnorlys.dk, security SSL, port 993; SMTP mail.mailnorlys.dk, security type 'Ingen' (none), port 587. The only documented SMTP endpoint is unencrypted, so no SMTP endpoint can be recorded and the row is unknown (the documented IMAP endpoint would be mail.mailnorlys.dk:993:tls:addr); the page links webmail.stofa.dk and webmail.norlys.dk and never names the address domain; stofanet.dk (and bbsyd.dk) as the address domain comes only from the third-party https://univik.com/email-settings/stofa.html (read 2026-10-05), which gives a different host (mail.stofanet.dk: IMAP 993 SSL, SMTP 587 STARTTLS, full address), contradicting the official host name; the Wayback Machine (to look for older Stofa pages) was offline on 2026-10-05; selection: next big Danish ISP after YouSee (used)

column1: sol.dk
column6: https://www.sol.dk/faq (read 2026-10-05, embedded FAQ data): answer to the mail-program question: incoming Vaertsnavn mail.sol.dk, Brugernavn = your @sol.dk e-mail address, server port 993, SSL: On; outgoing smtp.sol.dk, same username, port 465, SSL: On; authentication required, SPA no; no 143 or 587 named (not recorded); 'Hvem ejer Sol.dk?': Inbox.com AS, a Norwegian company; https://www.mailcore.com/en/ (read 2026-10-05): the ISP and portal mail platform MailCore (whose Danish infrastructure stores Inbox.com mail per https://www.inbox.com/faq/technical) lists SOL.dk as a customer case; selection: Danish portal mail provider; note: one HTTPS GET on port 443 to mail.sol.dk was made on 2026-10-05 while looking for the site's help pages, it redirected to www.sol.dk; caveat: same operator and template as wemail.no, inbox.com and inet.fi

column1: inet.fi
column6: https://www.inet.fi/faq (read 2026-10-05, embedded FAQ data): answer to the mail-program question: incoming Isantanimi mail.inet.fi, Kayttajatunnus = your @inet.fi address, port 993 with SSL/TLS (or 143 with STARTTLS); outgoing smtp.inet.fi, same username, port 465 with SSL/TLS (or 587 with STARTTLS), authentication required; 'Kuka omistaa Inet.fi:n?': owned by the Norwegian company Inbox.com AS; another answer says inet.fi used to be free from Telia, Telia stopped offering the free service and it is now a paid subscription (no subscription, no mailbox); another answer says mail from addresses not ending in inet.fi must be sent through smtp.tele.fi (Telia, not recorded); selection: Telia Finland's consumer mail, Finland's third big operator after Elisa (saunalahti.fi) and DNA (dnainternet.net), both used; other legacy Telia/Sonera domains not checked; caveat: same operator and template as wemail.no, inbox.com and sol.dk

https://1984.hosting/knowledge-base/email/ (read 2026-10-05): 'General Email Settings': IMAP mail.1984.is port 993 SSL/TLS, POP3 995 SSL/TLS, SMTP mail.1984.is 'Port 465 (SSL) or 587 (STARTTLS)', authentication required, 'Use your full email and password'; the Outlook 2007 and 2013 guides say username = your full email address, incoming and outgoing mail.1984.is, IMAP 993 SSL/TLS, SMTP 465 SSL/TLS or 587 STARTTLS; the guides call it 'your 1984.is email' and addresses are created on the customer's domains in the control panel, so mail.1984.is is one fixed host for all hosted domains; https://1984.hosting/ (read 2026-10-05): hosting in Icelandic data centers; that 1984's own 1984.is addresses use the same host is assumed; selection: Icelandic web host with documented mail (rank not verified)

column1: internet.is
column6: Syn (formerly Vodafone Iceland; vodafone.is now redirects to syn.is, seen 2026-10-05) mail: https://syn.is/verdskra/vefhysing-og-tolvupostur (price list, read 2026-10-05) sells 'Postholf @internet.is' mailboxes (1,290 kr./month, half price with Syn internet) and links its webmail at postur.internet.is (not visited); the settings help page https://syn.is/adstod/stillingar (read 2026-10-05) loads its articles client-side and the served HTML and embedded data contain no IMAP or SMTP text; web searches found no official IMAP/SMTP settings (one third-party wiki snippet naming an SMTP host for Vodafone Iceland was not read or used); selection: Iceland's next big telco after Siminn (simnet.is, used)
